Name: switch-in-match-arms

func f(x: i32) -> i32
    return match x
        #switch
            #case true
                1 => 1
        _ => 0
Console.writeLine("\(f(1))")
Intended: a #switch in a match arm list is reported once and skipped with its Case Group

Name: keyword-attribute-name
Source:
#match
func f() => ()
f()
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: a reserved word after '#' is no attribute Name; it is reported once, and the construct it would start is not read

Name: keyword-attribute-name-block
Source:
#match
    #case _
        Console.writeLine("x")
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: an indented body after a reserved word that ends the line of '#' would be the construct's that word starts, so it is skipped with it

Name: modifier-own-line
Source:
group G
    public
    func f() => ()
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: modifiers share the line of the word that introduces their declaration (Appendix F.3); modifiers that end their line introduce nothing and the declaration is missing after them

Name: modifier-before-directive
Intended: a directive is an item of its own (Appendix F.8): modifiers before it introduce nothing

Name: modifier-before-switch-line
Source:
public
#switch
    #case true
        func f() => ()
f()
Intended: a modifier on the line before a #switch introduces nothing; the Case Group is read as usual

Name: static-repeated
Source:
group G
    static static func f() => ()
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: each static is reported where it is read (SPEC 6.1), and a repetition is not a duplicate modifier as well

Name: open-before-access
Source:
open public struct S
    let x: i32
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: open immediately precedes struct (SPEC 6.2.2)

Name: open-on-init
Source:
open struct S
    let x: i32
    open init(x: i32)
        self.x = x
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: open before an init is reported once, where it is read; the constructor's own header check does not report it again

Name: attribute-after-modifier
Source:
public #Inline func t() => ()
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: attributes precede a declaration's modifiers (Appendix F.3): one after them is misplaced and marks nothing

Name: attribute-before-parameter-closer
Intended: attributes before the closer of a parameter list precede no parameter: its Name was expected there

Name: attribute-only-parameter
Source:
func f(#Layout(C)) -> i32 => 1
Console.writeLine("\(f())")
Intended: an attribute alone in a parameter list attaches to nothing, neither to the result Type nor to the body

Name: attribute-before-enum-case
Source:
enum E
    #Layout(C)
    A
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: an enum Case takes no attributes (SPEC 6.5); the attribute is reported and marks nothing

Name: attribute-before-constraint
Source:
struct S<T>
    #Foo
    T is Copy
    let x: i32
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: a Constraint takes no attributes; the attribute is reported, not judged as part of the subject Type

Name: attribute-before-body-constraint
Source:
func f<T>(x: T) -> ()
    #Foo
    T is Copy
    return
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: a body's Constraint prefix takes no attributes

Name: attribute-before-associate
Source:
contract C
    #Foo
    associate Item
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: an associate declaration takes no attributes

Name: attribute-on-requirement-parameter
Intended: an attribute misplaced before a requirement's Name is reported once; the receiver it is kept on is not a parameter with an attribute

Name: attribute-in-accessor-list
Source:
struct S
    var x: i32
        #Foo get
        set
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: an accessor list takes no attributes (SPEC 6.5); the attribute is reported and the accessor is still read

Name: attribute-on-constructor
Source:
struct S
    let x: i32
    #Foo
    init(x: i32)
        self.x = x
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: an init takes no attribute (SPEC 6.2.3); the header report keeps the attribute as its recovery, so it is not resolved

Name: static-own-line
Source:
group G
    static
    func f() => ()
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: a static that ends its line is reported once where it is read; being no modifier, it leaves no declaration missing after it

Name: modifier-line-before-body
Intended: an indented body after modifiers that end their line would be the missing declaration's, so it is skipped with them, as after a failed header

Name: open-own-line
Source:
open
struct B
    let b: i32
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: an open that ends its line is a modifier without its declaration; the struct on the next line is declared without it

Name: duplicate-self-constraint-location
Source:
contract Marker
struct S
    Self is Marker
    let x: i32
struct S
    Self is Marker
    let y: i32
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: a second fragment's Constraint region is reported at its subject, not at the next line

Name: origin-relation-operator-missing
Source:
func f(a: ref/i32) -> i32
    origin a
    return 1
Console.writeLine("hi")
Intended: a relation whose line ends after its left operand misses its operator at the insertion point; the right operand, missing there too, rests on it
